title: Abstract Book: Day 2

headings.text: Low-cost turbidity sensors for estuary monitoring
Sampling design for patchy seagrass meadows
Quantifying uncertainty in sea-level projections for small ports
A hybrid wave model trained on buoy records
Communicating flood risk to coastal communities

key_sentences: We compare four low-cost turbidity sensors against a laboratory nephelometer over a six-month deployment.
The sensors agree within eight per cent after a simple temperature correction.
Seagrass cover is rarely uniform, so simple random sampling wastes effort.
We propose an adaptive design that adds samples where the variance is high.
Mapping the intertidal zone on foot is slow and limited by the tide.
We flew a small drone at low water and built elevation models with a vertical error below four centimetres.
Harbour authorities need sea-level projections with honest error bars.
We combine tide gauge records with regional ice-sheet scenarios and report the full range of outcomes.
Physical wave models are accurate but expensive to run for every harbour.

list_items.text: Print the poster at A0 size, portrait.
Bring four pins; the boards are cork.
Collect your lanyard at the registration desk.
